rust_authorities: A standalone Rust HTTP/SQLite runtime now directly owns account-session, clan, current-profile and public-history requests. It executes the shared native plans and typed source checks through the same safe Rust Owners registry used by the C ABI; there is no Python server/coordinator on these routes. The former FFI owner dispatcher moved verbatim into the unsafe-forbidden protocol crate and the bounded C ABI delegates to it. The Rust runtime owns its private SQLite connection, transaction/COMMIT/rollback, current Steam-grant SQL checks before canonical publication, native account reservation/grants, cache acknowledgements after commit, fixed HTTPS Discord application/scope/user verification, source/prefix/principal budgets, connection/header/body/work limits and cancellation-safe work leases. Real executable/HTTP checks cover malformed/duplicate input, wrong/expired/revoked grants, clan lifecycle/replay/presence, profile failed COMMIT/retry, public queries, logout and process restart; a native account client uses the actual Rust HTTP route with only its provider handoff replaced by a deterministic fixture. This is a partial service migration: full matchmaking readiness remains false and unported capabilities return503. Steam OpenID/pending/refresh issuance, accepted-party/queue/catalog/room/transport/EOS/social routes, complete endpoint/service replacement, cross-store/process coordination, original Live/history/arbitration recovery and the full native/delivered gates remain open. No selected runtime or production service is activated.
